method: Read-only review separated catalogue structure, source presence, action wording and escalation boundaries from transport availability.
Focused semantic sampling covered emergency recognition, first aid, medication safety, overdose, self-harm crisis and maternal mental health.
The prior v2.4.0 blocking cases were rechecked against the current text instead of inheriting the old report's result.
This is an editorial safety review, not a clinician signature, diagnosis, treatment validation or promise of real-time source freshness.

evidence: Sepsis now uses the dedicated CDC sepsis page and explicit immediate escalation language.
Cardiac arrest, adult choking and severe bleeding actions use ordered first-aid wording and avoid the prior concatenation errors.
Acute confusion, suicide crisis, severe hypoglycaemia and opioid overdose use topic-specific sources and explicit emergency boundaries.
Postpartum mental-health wording distinguishes urgent safety risks from prompt non-emergency assessment.

conditions: Keep the general-education disclaimer and local emergency-service boundary visible.
Do not claim clinician signoff or provide diagnosis, prescription or individualized treatment.
A future factual, source or safety correction is an allowed v2.5.x maintenance patch.
